critical_assertions.note: Misclosure of ~0.98 ft. Every figure matches the print (checked at 300 dpi). The inconsistency sits at the Lot 12 corner: the 85.00 ft tie along Washington Avenue plus courses (8) and (7) reversed (37.73 and 85.34 ft) end 0.785 ft off the Kings Highway West line. No single course explains it (the error vector, az 184.9°, aligns with no course), so no intended value is recorded.

common_failure_modes: Calls 6 and 8 share the same bearing (N 59°02' E) but run along different boundaries (Kings Highway West vs the Lot 12 line)
The notch formed by calls 6-7-8 where Lot 12 meets Lot 11.01 creates a concave boundary
The ~0.98 ft misclosure is in the deed's own figures; a parser reading the print cannot close it
notes: Checked against Book 9787 Pages 1784-1785, PDF pages 1-2 (300 dpi): the legal description, all eight courses, the point of beginning and deed_info match the print. Shared lines agree with the sibling deeds: 84.84, 13.35 and 58.57 ft with 7103-248 Tract Three and 164.01 ft with 7103-254. The 0.98 ft misclosure comes from the Lot 12 corner (the 85.00 ft tie, 37.73 and 85.34 ft miss the Kings Highway West line by 0.785 ft); no single misprint explains it. This is the main 8 Kings Highway West parcel (Lot 11.01), the L-shaped lot that wraps from Kings Highway West around to Washington Avenue. It was the commercial building parcel retained when the larger parcel was subdivided for the Willits Court townhouses. Sold in 2013 by 8 Kings Highway LLC to Kings Hall LLC for $522,000. The 8-sided shape results from: Washington Ave frontage (call 1), the notch boundary with the Willits Court lots (calls 2-3-4), the Lot 11 boundary (call 5), Kings Highway frontage (call 6), and the Lot 12 jog (calls 7-8). Legal description rebuilt 2026-10-31 from the recorded PDF (Book 9787 Pages 1784-1785, PDF pages 1-2); the previous text was a placeholder ("thence (1) through (8) to the point and place of beginning"). All eight courses match the deed as printed, so the ~0.98 ft misclosure is the deed's own.
